text:
Miss Harper had been the town librarian for forty years, and she had only one rule: “Return every book exactly as you found it.”

Many people thought the rule was strange. Some borrowers tried to argue with her. “Why does it matter? It’s just a book,” they said.

One day, a teenage boy named Felix borrowed a rare old book about astronomy. He read it in the park, and when he got up to leave, he accidentally left a coffee stain on the cover. He was afraid to return it. For three weeks, he kept the book hidden in his room.

Finally, he went back to the library with his head down. “Miss Harper, I damaged the book,” he said, and he explained everything.

To his surprise, she wasn’t angry. “Do you know why I have my rule?” she asked. “It isn’t about the book. It’s about respect. When you borrow something, you carry the trust of a person you may never meet. The next reader deserves to find what you found.”

She repaired the cover herself. Then she gave Felix a job in the library, shelving books on Saturdays.

Felix worked there for six years. Today, he is the head of a university library, and a small sign hangs behind his desk: “Return every book exactly as you found it.”

Moral: Respect what is lent to you, because someone else will need it after you.

quiz.q: Miss Harper had been the town librarian for forty years.
Miss Harper was very angry with Felix.
What was the book Felix borrowed about?
Return every book exactly as you ___ it.
